name: The Springs Resort & Spa
positioning: Hot springs resort facing the Arenal Volcano, with its own riverside adventure center and wildlife preserve
best_for: Families and groups who want river adventures and wildlife without leaving the property
Couples who want volcano views and hot spring soaks

facts.text: The resort is in La Fortuna, Costa Rica, directly north of the Arenal Volcano.
The resort has a view of the Arenal Volcano and natural hot springs.
Hot springs, pools and waterfalls are spread across the property, some tucked into the jungle and others connected to a swim-up bar.
The water in the hydrothermal pools rises naturally from volcanic magma far below ground.
Every guest room, suite and villa has a private terrace or balcony with a view of the volcano.
Rooms are equipped with hammocks, rocking chairs, minibars and marble bathrooms with Jacuzzi tubs.
The Sanctuary Spa uses the resort's own thermal mineral springs in its therapies.
The Sanctuary Spa takes up one entire level of the reception building.
Club Rio offers river tubing, river kayaking, horseback riding, a climbing and rappelling wall, an animal sanctuary, guided nature hikes, fishing and hot springs.
The horseback ride crosses the Arenal River and gallops through mountain meadows facing the Arenal Volcano.
A guided night walk through the jungle looks for tree frogs, scorpions and two-toed sloths.
The chef uses organic fruits and vegetables grown for the resort on neighboring farms.

highlights.text: Club Rio Outdoor Center sits below the resort along a forested, mile-long stretch of Arenal River frontage.
With Costa Rica's Ministry of Environment and Energy, the resort runs a preserve for wildlife confiscated from poachers or donated by reserves, rescue centers or individuals.
The Honeymoon Vista Guest Room has a garden terrace with a private hot spring-fed Jacuzzi.
Las Hojas Spa Bungalow is in a river canyon surrounded by several hot springs and creeks.
La Laguna swim-up bar sits in the center of the largest lagoon pool, which has infinity-edge waterfalls facing the volcano.

considerations.text: Club Rio is about a mile from the main lobby, reached by a shuttle that runs every half hour.
Club Rio has no lifeguards or babysitters, so parents must supervise children there.
Room rates do not include breakfast or other meals.
